A4.question: Which #513 profile supplies F0702, and how do F0702 and the #492 profile link?
A4.proposed_answer: F0702 has no independent producer. It is a value copy of F0193, which the route already assigns to the #513 trailing-window rate projection (share-rate variant of the raw rolling return/share-rate/rate-difference role). The #513 rate projection divides a window sum by the window length and consumes the #492 plain rolling trade-window volume profile (not the tick-signed profile); #513 already lists #492 as a prerequisite. Recommend recording F0702 as an alias of F0193 (duplicate profile, identical value) and naming it as the supplied raw rate operand of #626.
residual: window-end convention and empty-window behavior are not frozen
EF4 producer versus EF3 consumer: per wave 1 B7 the value enters #626 as a supplied operand through I/O, so no EF4 production edge for EF3 acceptance

B2.question: What do F0700, F0701 and F0721 carry and who produces them?
B2.proposed_answer: F0700 is the entity identity echoed from the input observation. F0701 is the input observation event clock echoed from the input; it is also an ordering operand (an update applies only if its clock advances for the entity and session). F0721 is the nested session-summary aggregate holding the computed session-summary outputs F0690 to F0699. So F0700 and F0701 are supplied facts: #611 maps them, #626 must name them as input identity and ordering operands in its contract. F0721 is a computed #626 output group that #611 only envelopes. Proposed re-attribution of the primary owner: F0721 to #626; F0700 and F0701 to supplied-operand status with #611 as mapping and #626 as consumer. The serialized carrier F0179 stays with #570.
B2.confidence: medium-high for F0700 and F0701; medium for F0721
residual: #626 contract has not stated whether the session-summary group is emitted per update or at session end
reset-on-new-session semantics belong to the #626 contract

B5.question: Which observed-population companion outputs does #598 need, and who produces their operands?
B5.proposed_answer: Seven draft outputs, kept under distinct observed-population names so denominators are never mixed with declared-universe outputs: (1) qualifying observed member count; (2) observed advancing member count (strictly positive change); (3) observed advance fraction = (2)/(1), which is not the advance/decline ratio because non-advancing members are not split; (4) to (6) the same three per supplied group label together with group size; (7) a per-cohort and per-group coverage record (observed members, no expected population). Regime classification, cut-offs, score scaling and projection of the cohort result onto each member stay in #518. Operand producers: per-member change F0206 (delivered candidates, #507 route), eligibility inputs F0150 and F0161 with caller floors (delivered candidates), group label F0255 (delivered #508 candidate), identity F0137 (delivered). The consumer counts duplicates of an identity while the rank consumers keep one value per identity, so duplicate-identity handling must be frozen once. Placement: either retitle and extend #598 with a separately versioned observed-population profile or number a narrow companion story; this is an owner decision.
B5.confidence: medium for the output list; low-medium for the placement
residual: whether a declared-universe profile may later reuse the same arithmetic

B6.question: Which adaptive outputs do S0336, S0337 and S0357 consume?
B6.proposed_answer: All three read the session-summary group F0721 (carried by F0179) and the session change F0206 for direction, plus caller thresholds. S0336 consumes the acceleration-diagnostic episode count F0695 and peak score F0696. S0337 consumes the baseline-availability flag F0699, the trigger count F0694 and the composite peak score F0690. S0357 consumes F0699 and the peak short-window relative volume F0692. Transitive #626 inputs: the supplied raw rate F0702 (all three families through the minimum-rate gate and the acceleration diagnostic), the relative-volume window values and availability flags F0208 to F0211 (route #490, EF3), F0186 and F0700. Proposed output-level edges: #518 to #626 for exactly these six outputs plus the envelope; the #519 optional edge covers the same set only if #519 re-derives them, otherwise it is unnecessary for these three rows. The private source profile for these rows names #490 as numerical owner; it predates #626 and is superseded by decision D-FLIP.
B6.confidence: medium-high for the consumed outputs; medium for the transitive list
residual: thresholds are caller parameters and are not defaulted
#626 contract must state when the session summary is final
